annotation.title_clean: AI, Big Data and rare diseases (exploratory opinion requested by the Danish Presidency of the Council of the EU)
annotation.title_en: AI, Big Data and rare diseases (exploratory opinion requested by the Danish Presidency of the Council of the EU)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C series
annotation.summary_en: European Economic and Social Committee exploratory opinion, requested by the Danish Presidency, on AI and Big Data in rare diseases. It recommends digitising health data, patient consent and data control, mandatory physician oversight and explainability, gender-balanced training data, SME funding, training, and EU-wide ethical guidelines for healthcare AI. Embodied AI appears only in passing (exoskeletons).
key_provisions_or_claims: Member States should give AI models access only to anonymised, encrypted patient data under EHDS, with sanctions for misuse.
EMA should require explainability and mandatory physician oversight for AI-based healthcare decisions.
AI Office should promote gender-diverse training data, bias audits and pre-market gender testing for medical AI.
Fund SMEs and startups via Horizon Europe and create a publicly funded AI diagnostic platform under EU4Health.
Establish EU-wide ethical guidelines for AI in healthcare and AI literacy and training programmes.
